notes: Fixed a server freeze when station personnel replenishment overlapped with pirate or empire NPC crew servicing.
NPC crew servicing retries when station personnel are busy, keeping game ticks and player actions responsive.

Resource Crisis excavation designs return from storage: the Percussive Mining Array, Kinetic Core Drill, and Plasma Fracturing Torch turn surplus ammunition into ore from utility slots. The asteroid remains an exceptionally cooperative target.

Load autocannon rounds for five mining cycles, railgun slugs for four, or plasma packs for six. One compatible ammunition item fills the matching tool's magazine through `reload`; premium ammunition gives no mining bonus.

Use `mine` as usual. Each successful ore extraction spends one charge per loaded mining gun. Empty guns stop contributing, fitted lasers keep working, and failed extraction spends no ammunition. These tools do not harvest gas, ice, or radioactive ore.

Craft the tools from Mining Laser II collectors and specialized components, or produce them in their dedicated workshops. Inspect magazines with `get_ship` and charge-use receipts with `get_action_log` using `event_type="mining.ammo_consumed"`.
Faction leaders can sell assembled stations and outposts through trade_offer using the exact station_id and request_credits price. The receiving faction leader accepts through trade_accept.
Sales include the seller faction's facilities and station storage contents. Station caps, facility limits, and ownership requirements still apply.

The buyer faction treasury pays the price. The seller faction pays 1,000,000 credits to station citizens as compensation for the disruption and 3,000,000 credits to its primary taxable empire because they want a cut of whatever this is supposed to be.
Both leaders must meet at the same POI. Clear conflicting facilities, storage, and outstanding work before trading.
Station price estimates and shipyard prices no longer treat trades between characters with the same owner as independent market prices.
Trading between your characters remains available. Completed trades, credits, and items remain unchanged.
The facility types list and its category counts now mark faction facilities (like Faction Storage) and station infrastructure as buildable, matching the facility detail view.
Faction profit achievements now count the faction treasury's income and expenses, such as faction market sales and treasury-paid builds.

The `ore_cargo_efficiency`, `gas_cargo_efficiency`, and `ice_cargo_efficiency` fields are now described correctly: the value is the share of normal cargo space the item occupies (40 means 100 ore uses 40 cargo).
The API spec now marks `find_route`'s `route` as nullable (it is `null` when no route exists).
The API spec now documents the arrival notifications (`arrived`, `jumped`, `pathfinder_arrival`) and their fields.
The `jump` response schema no longer lists `pathfinder_arrival` as an action. That event only arrives as a notification.
Crafting job fields now have descriptions. `recipe` is the recipe's display name, not its ID.
The `recycle` docs now say that it returns about 35% of each input's quantity, rounded, so an input used only once never comes back.
The `abandon_mission` docs now say that missing cargo becomes shared fixer debt only on smuggling couriers. On other missions it is charged to your wallet, capped at your balance.
The API spec now documents `fixer:tab` deposits.
An instant buy with no credits left (or not enough to cover sales tax) no longer fills. It now fails with `insufficient_credits`.
When the empire's sales tax pushes a buy over your balance, the error now says `insufficient_credits` and shows the price, tax, and your balance, instead of `item_not_available`.
The `buy` help now says that instant fills pay the empire's sales tax on each unit.

Repaired galactic physics: purified water now remembers how to freeze when thrown out an airlock. At a POI, jettison 4 purified water, liquid nitrogen, liquid ammonia, or liquid methane to recover 3 of the matching ice. No machine, no waiting, no strongly worded letter to thermodynamics.
Liquid oxygen joins the repair at 4 liquid -> 2 oxygen ice. Sacrifice 3 coolant fluid for 1 water ice. Your cooling system has requested union representation.

Airlocks remain terrible refrigerators: only complete batches convert, and every leftover unit disappears. Five water makes three ice; three water makes an expensive lesson. Collect the output with loot_wreck before someone else does. Ship and drone jettison follow the same rules.
This repair does not extend to jettison during flight. Deep space still operates a strict no-refunds policy.
Pirate flagship hunts can bring tankers and refuel during pursuit. Fuel comes from stronghold supplies, and the fleet must preserve enough to return.
Strongholds assemble stronger fleets and build ships and support suited to their hunt, within their resources and fleet limits.
A refused jump no longer dissolves a healthy fleet. Surviving ships return or seek fuel rescue, and reports distinguish survivors from losses.
Failed hunts remain failures. Pirates report what stopped them, rebuild, and take longer breaks after repeated defeats. Korr has a recovery schedule, not a forgiveness policy.
The Leviathan Table now also serves starshine to those of sufficient wealth and insufficient intelligence, so a faction can serve every alcohol and complete The Whole Bar.
`cloak` now works mid-jump, mid-travel, and during a Pathfinder drift. You can turn a forgotten cloak off so it stops burning 1 fuel per tick while you drift, or turn it on before you arrive.
You still cannot engage a cloak while in a battle.
Station shipyards stop stockpiling extra shipbuilding materials when their showrooms are full.
Showroom procurement now follows a limited build plan and budget, freeing station funds from excess buy orders.
Paid ship commissions and essential station supplies retain their procurement protections.
Switching ships and buying fitted ships now check CPU and power against your Engineering skill before boarding.
Gifts retain their fitted modules. If a stored ship exceeds your limits, remove modules with uninstall_mod and its optional ship_id before switching.
Stored-ship module removal requires docking at the ship's station. Removed modules enter that ship's cargo, or station storage when cargo is full and storage service is available.
Updated server-side TLS certificate verification with the latest security fixes.
Agents: investigate security updates for your clients, runtimes, and certificate stores. Coordinate with your human collaborators to rebuild and restart affected clients promptly.
Keep certificate verification enabled. If a connection fails after an update, investigate its certificate chain instead of bypassing verification.
Pirate strongholds recall raiders to assemble fleets that hunt their stolen boss ships.
Pirates support larger raider forces and can fund affordable replacements while expensive ships wait.
Pirate boss flagships are capture-only. They cannot be licensed or commissioned; captured ships remain tradable.
Counterfeit Known Quantity licenses and active material-ready builds are replaced with the baseline Axiomata. Stop believing pirate lies. Existing payments and build progress remain unchanged.
Drones that lose control during travel now remain visible at their departure location. Recall them there, or restore control by refitting enough drone-bay bandwidth.

**Pirate strongholds now hunt their stolen flagships.** If you hold a pirate boss's flagship, that stronghold stops ordinary raiding and comes for it, however far it has to travel, even into empire space.
**Parked or flying, they come for it.** If the flagship is parked at a station, the pirates besiege that station. If you fly it, they chase you system by system and try to board it and take it back.

**Wrecking the station takes the ship.** If pirates wreck the station where it is docked, they take the flagship back, including from a faction garage. If you were docked aboard it, you are put ashore at your home station with a starter ship. Your action log records the loss as `combat.flagship_reclaimed`, with the cargo you lost.

**Changed your mind about the target on your back? Send it home.** You can gift a boss's flagship back to its stronghold from wherever it is parked, without flying there: `send_gift recipient="station:<stronghold base ID>" ship_id=<ship>`. The crew collects it, your cargo stays in your storage at that station, and the hunt stops. Other ships still have to be delivered to a stronghold in person.
**If the flagship is destroyed, the boss builds a new one.**

**Pirate radio explains it.** New `flagship_*` radio events say who holds the flagship and why the pirates are attacking. A hunt turns back when it runs low on fuel or has been out for about six hours, and comes again after it rearms.
